title: Money & currency
body:
Currency is the Japanese yen (¥). Tokyo is more card-friendly than its reputation, but small izakaya, ramen ticket machines, and some traditional spots remain cash- or IC-card-only — carry cash as backup.

Seven Bank (7-Eleven) ATMs are the most reliable for foreign cards: 24/7, 28,000+ locations nationwide, and they accept Visa/Plus, Mastercard/Maestro/Cirrus, UnionPay, Amex, JCB, Discover and Diners Club. Per-withdrawal limit is {{fact:atm-withdrawal-limit-100000-yen}}.

Tax-free shopping still runs on the old instant-discount system for this trip — Japan's switch to a refund-at-departure system starts November 1, 2026, after you've left.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Per-person estimates for a food-focused trip. Casual-day food and local transport are aggregator-sourced ranges (⚠ not a single official figure); the Saturday anchor dinner figure is RyuGin's own published course price + service charge. Lodging is left at zero — accommodation style wasn't set at intake.
